1.concept: 不定式 — Causative verb 'make' + bare infinitive
1.zh: 妈妈让俊杰把盘子里的蔬菜吃掉。
1.note: make + 宾语 + 动词原形（使役动词），不用 eats/eating。

2.concept: 量词 — Quantifier with uncountable noun (negative sentence)
2.zh: “我们家没有多少家具，刚装修完。”她解释道。
2.note: furniture 不可数，用 much；a few/many 接可数复数。

3.concept: 主谓一致 — Subject–verb agreement with 'One of …'
3.zh: “其中一个男孩已经去请校长了。”老师解释道。
3.note: One of + 复数名词，谓语用单数 has；表示已去未回常用 has gone。

4.concept: 关系词 — Object relative pronoun for people
4.zh: 生日会后，苏珊给想感谢的朋友们写信。
4.note: 介词后指人用 whom；friends 为先行词。

5.concept: 代词 — Object pronoun in compound object
5.zh: 考试结束后，爸爸给我妹妹和我买了冰淇淋作奖励。
5.note: 介词 for 后接宾格 me；不用 I。

6.concept: 主谓一致 — Subject–verb agreement — 'Either … or …' (proximity rule)
6.zh: 要么爱玲要么她父母稍后会去市场买菜。
6.note: Either … or … 谓语与较近主语一致，parents 为复数，用 are going。

7.concept: 条件句 — Conditional connector — 'Unless' (= If … not)
7.zh: 除非拉朱得到父母同意，否则不能参加班级郊游。
7.note: Unless = if not，引导条件；Since/As long as 语气不同。

8.concept: 现在完成时 — Present perfect continuous — ongoing action up to now
8.zh: “我每天放学后一直在练钢琴，所以相信能在即将到来的演奏会发挥好。”苏茜说。
8.note: 从过去持续到现在的练习，用现在完成进行 have been practising。

9.concept: 反意疑问句 — Question tag — 'rarely' is a negative adverb
9.note: rarely 表否定意义，附加疑问用肯定 does she。

10.concept: 固定介词 — Fixed preposition — 'under treatment'
10.zh: 病人正在接受感染治疗。
10.note: 固定搭配 under treatment for …。

cloze: The electric eel gets its name from its ability to generate electricity. Specialised organs within its body [Q16 (generate)] powerful electric shocks of up to 650 volts. Despite having this ability, electric eels are not naturally threatening. They use their electric shocks mainly to stun their prey and [Q17 (deter)] predators.

Electric eels are nocturnal and are most active at night. [Q18 (Residing)] in murky, dark waters, they have poor vision. Rather than relying on their sight, they give out weak electric signals that function like radar, allowing them to find their prey. Upon finding smaller fish, they send a [Q19 (significantly)] stronger shock to prevent their catch from escaping.
How strong can an electric eel's shock be? Well, the shock of an electric eel has been known to knock a horse off its feet. Truly, it is an astonishing [Q20 (feat)]!
zh: 电鳗得名于其发电能力。体内特化器官可产生高达650伏的强大电击。尽管有此能力，电鳗并非天生具有威胁性，主要用电击击晕猎物并驱赶捕食者。
电鳗昼伏夜出，夜间最活跃。它们栖息于浑浊昏暗的水域，视力很差。与其依赖视觉，它们发出弱电信号，像雷达一样运作，帮助找到猎物。发现小鱼后，它们会发出明显更强的电击，防止猎物逃脱。
电鳗的电击能有多强？已知其电击曾把一匹马击倒在地。的确是一项惊人的本领！

options.3: It highlights bringing family members together.
options.4: It focuses on the need to build a strong community.

21.concept: 题型 — Image–text link — 'connect under the stars'（题型考点）
21.note: under the stars means in the open at night, so the supporting image should literally show people outdoors with the sky visible → (3) people sitting under the open sky. (1) picnic, (2) cosy room (indoors), and (4) feast all miss the open-sky cue.

22.concept: 标题 — Genre inference from movie title（标题考点）
22.note: Movie title: The Mystery of Maplewood Manor. The keyword Mystery + a manor setting strongly suggests a suspenseful, mystery/thriller film → (1) a thriller. (2) fantasy would imply magic/imaginary worlds; (3) comedy would be light-hearted; (4) documentary is non-fiction.

23.concept: 细节 — Detail check — admission price（信息定位）
23.note: Poster: Adult tickets at $5. Complimentary tickets for children! — children pay nothing → (4). (1) only popcorn and one drink are free, not free-flow beverages for adults; (2) registration must be online by 23 October, not on the spot; (3) family attendance is not required.

24.concept: 目的 — Author's purpose — promote a community event（目的考点）
24.note: The poster is from the Willow Movie Lovers Club and invites people to register and turn up at Willow Park — its main purpose is to draw audiences to that local event → (2). (1) is too general (about more movies in life); (3) the poster gives event details, not movie review information; (4) spending time with loved ones is implied but not the primary purpose.

25.concept: 题型 — Cross-text link — family time as the shared theme（题型考点）
25.note: Poster's tagline Bring your loved ones aligns most directly with Text 2's central message that family time strengthens bonds → (3). (1) lists indoor and outdoor activities, but the poster only describes one outdoor event; (2) games are only one example in Text 2; (4) 'strong community' is the bigger backdrop but the poster's pull is on the family unit, not the whole community.

cloze: Jellyfish can be found in oceans all around the world. [Q26] creatures have bell-shaped bodies and long tentacles that make them fascinating and mysterious. [Q27] jellyfish do not have a brain, heart or bones, some species can be highly dangerous to humans.

A jellyfish sting happens when [Q28] tentacles make contact with the skin. These tentacles contain tiny barbs that inject venom which may cause pain, swelling or [Q29] serious allergic reactions. Box jellyfish, for example, are among the most venomous marine creatures and have been known to cause fatalities [Q30] extreme cases.

In Singapore, jellyfish sightings and stings are reported more frequently [Q31] the warmer months. These happen particularly at popular beaches like Sentosa and East Coast Park. Lifeguards stationed [Q32] these beaches are trained to manage such situations calmly and quickly. [Q33] a person is stung, it is crucial not to scratch or rub the affected area as this could cause the venom to spread.
Medical experts advise that the sting should be rinsed with vinegar and [Q34] soaked in warm water to ease the pain. In more urgent cases, emergency medical attention must be sought without delay.
[Q35] their beauty, jellyfish should be observed from a safe distance. With the right precautions, a trip to the beach can still be safe and enjoyable.
zh: 水母可以在世界各地的海洋中找到。这些生物拥有钟形的身体和长长的触手，使它们既迷人又神秘。虽然水母没有大脑、心脏或骨头，但有些品种对人类来说仍然非常危险。
当水母的触手接触到皮肤时，就会发生蛰伤。这些触手上长着细小的倒钩，会注入毒液，可能引起疼痛、肿胀，甚至严重的过敏反应。例如，箱形水母是最具毒性的海洋生物之一，在极端情况下甚至会导致死亡。
在新加坡，气候较暖的几个月里，水母的目击和蛰伤报告更为频繁。这些情况特别容易发生在像圣淘沙和东海岸公园这样的热门海滩。驻守在这些海滩上的救生员都受过训练，能够冷静而迅速地处理这类情况。如果一个人被蛰，关键是不要抓挠或揉搓受影响的部位，否则可能会让毒液扩散。
医学专家建议，被蛰处应先用醋冲洗，然后浸泡在温水中以减轻疼痛。在更紧急的情况下，必须毫不拖延地寻求紧急医疗援助。
尽管水母十分美丽，但仍应从安全距离观察它们。只要采取正确的防范措施，去海滩的行程仍然可以既安全又愉快。

26.note: these creatures = 这些生物（水母）。

27.note: Although jellyfish do not have a brain … = 尽管没有大脑等器官。

28.note: its tentacles make contact = 它的触手接触皮肤。

29.note: even serious allergic reactions = 甚至严重过敏。

30.note: fatalities in extreme cases = 在极端情况下致死。

31.note: during the warmer months = 在较暖的几个月。

32.note: stationed at these beaches = 驻守在这些海滩。

33.note: If a person is stung = 若有人被蛰。

35.note: Despite their beauty = 尽管美丽仍须远观。

cloze: Nowadays, modern entertainment revolves around screens and social media. My own childhood was shaped [Q36(with)] simple, [Q37(tradishional)] games. These were moments of unfiltered joy, spent [Q38(to)] the company of neighbours who gradually [Q39(become)] lifelong friends.

Among the many games we played, five stones stood out for its [Q40(desepteve)] simplicity. What began as a casual pastime quickly became a contest of skill and precision. I remember spending countless afternoons practising the art of tossing and catching those bean bags, [Q41(determination)] to master every level.

Another game was zero point that [Q42(rekwired)] agility, timing, and a fair amount of courage. As the elastic rope rose higher with each round, so did the stakes — and the laughter. Failure [Q43(were)] met with good-natured teasing, and victory with loud cheers.

In [Q44(hionsight)] , those games did more than occupy our time. They nurtured [Q45(risiliense)] , cooperation, and a sense of community. These are the qualities that no digital game can ever truly replicate.
zh: 如今，现代娱乐主要围绕着屏幕和社交媒体展开。而我自己的童年则是由那些简单的传统游戏所塑造的。那是充满纯粹欢乐的时光，是在邻居们的陪伴中度过的，他们也渐渐成为我一生的朋友。
在我们玩过的众多游戏中，五颗石子因其看似简单却另有玄机的特点尤其令人难忘。原本只是随意的消遣，很快就变成了一场比拼技巧与准确度的较量。我记得自己用了无数个下午练习抛接那些豆袋的技巧，下定决心要征服每一关。
另一项游戏叫做“零点”，它需要敏捷、时机感和相当的勇气。随着每一轮橡皮绳越拉越高，挑战和笑声也水涨船高。失败时大家会善意地互相打趣，胜利时则迎来阵阵欢呼。
回头看，那些游戏远不止是消磨时间。它们培养了我们的韧性、合作精神，以及对社区的归属感。这些品质是任何电子游戏都无法真正复制的。

36.note: my childhood was shaped with simple, traditional games → by. The passive verb was shaped takes its agent with the preposition by (shaped by N), not with. With would introduce a tool, not the doer/cause.

37.note: tradishional → traditional. The suffix is -tional (cf. national, additional, optional), spelt with t + i + onal; the /ʃ/ sound is hidden in the ti, never written as sh in this word family.

38.note: spent to the company of neighbours → in. The fixed phrase is in the company of N = together with someone. To the company is not idiomatic English.

39.note: The narrator is reflecting on childhood; the surrounding verbs are past (was shaped, were moments, spent). So gradually become lifelong friends must shift to past simple → became.

40.note: desepteve → deceptive (= misleadingly simple). Stem decept- + suffix -ive. Common error: spelling /s/ as se instead of ce, and -ive as -eve.

41.concept: Word form — adjective for participial phrase
41.note: practising the art of tossing and catching those bean bags, determination to master every level — the slot needs an adjective describing the writer (the implied subject of the participial clause), not the abstract noun → determined. Pattern: S + V, determined + to V = resolved to do something.

42.note: rekwired → required. Latin-origin spelling: re- + quire (the /kw/ sound is always written qu, never kw, in Latin-derived words like require, request, quiet).

43.note: Failure were met with good-natured teasing → was. Failure here is uncountable (= the experience of failing in general), so it takes a singular verb. (Plural Failures + were would also work, but the question asks us to correct the existing word.)

44.note: hionsight → hindsight = looking back at past events. Compound of hind (= behind, after) + sight (= seeing). Common error: writing hion- for hind-.

45.note: risiliense → resilience (= ability to recover quickly). Stem resilient → noun resilience. Common errors: writing risi- for resi- and -ense for -ence (compare patient → patience, not patiense).

cloze: Have you ever stopped to think about where your bowl of rice comes from? As ordinary as it may seem, rice is one of the [Q46] important food crops in the world. It feeds more than half of the world's population every day.

Rice is believed to have been first [Q47] in China over 9,000 years ago. Since its cultivation, it has spread [Q48] Asia, Africa, and the Americas. Today, it is grown in more than one hundred countries [Q49] India, Indonesia, and Vietnam. Rice plants are typically grown in wet, muddy fields called paddies, [Q50] allow them to thrive.

There are many different [Q51] of rice, but they generally fall into two categories — long grain and short grain. Basmati rice from India and Jasmine rice from Thailand are long-grain types. They are [Q52] for their fragrant aroma. On the other hand, Japanese sushi rice is short-grain and becomes sticky when cooked.

Rice has [Q53] uses. In Asia, it is often steamed and served with meat or vegetables. In Spain, rice is cooked [Q54] seafood over a huge pan and in Japan, it is shaped into sushi. Even in desserts, rice [Q55] a key role in dishes like rice pudding or sweet glutinous rice cakes.

Aside from being a source of carbohydrates, rice also provides protein and essential vitamins. Brown rice is often considered [Q56] than white rice as it has not been polished and is higher in minerals and fibers. [Q57], both are great sources of energy.

Rice is more than just food — it is a [Q58] part of many cultures and traditions. In weddings across Asia, rice may be thrown to wish the couple prosperity. During [Q59], special rice dishes are prepared to honour ancestors and celebrate harvests.
The next time you see a bowl of rice, remember that it is not [Q60] a simple grain. It feeds billions and connects cultures across the globe.
zh: 你可曾想过碗里那勺饭从何而来？米饭看似平常，却是世界上最重要的粮食作物之一，每天养活全球一半以上人口。
据信稻米约九千多年前首次在中国栽培，此后传播至亚洲、非洲与美洲；如今在一百多个国家种植，如印度、印尼与越南。水稻通常种在称为稻田的湿润泥田，有利于生长。
稻米品种繁多，大致分长粒与短粒；印度香米与泰国茉莉香米为长粒，以香气著称；日本寿司米为短粒，煮熟后黏。
稻米用途广泛：亚洲常蒸饭配菜；西班牙用大盘与海鲜同煮；日本做成寿司；甜点里米饭也扮演要角，如米布丁、糯米糕。
除碳水化合物外，稻米还提供蛋白质与必需维生素；糙米因未精磨、矿物质与纤维较高，常被认为比白米更健康；不过两者都是良好能量来源。
稻米不仅是食物，也是许多文化传统的重要部分：亚洲婚礼有时撒米祝福新人；节庆期间会准备特色米食祭祖、庆祝丰收。
下次见到一碗饭，请记住它不只是简单谷物——它养活数十亿人，也把全球文化联结在一起。

46.note: 构成最高级结构 one of the most important，用以形容稻米是世界上“最重要”的粮食作物之一。

47.note: 与前文 has been 构成被动语态，结合后文 cultivation（耕作/栽培），表示稻米最初在九千年前被“种植”或“驯化”（cultivated/grown/domesticated）。

48.note: 动词 spread 后接介词，表示稻米的种植在亚洲、非洲及美洲大陆“广泛传播”或“传遍”（across/throughout）。

49.note: 用于引出具体的国家例子（印度、印尼和越南），填入 like 或是与 such 联用构成 such as 均可。

50.concept: 非限制性定语从句引导词
50.note: 非限制性定语从句，逗号后需要填入关系代词 which 指代先行词 paddies（稻田），并在从句中作主语。

51.note: 后文提到长粒米和短粒米两大类别，此空格指大米有许多不同的“种类”或“品种”（types/varieties/kinds）。

52.concept: 被动语态固定习惯搭配
52.note: 构成固定搭配 be known for 或 be famous for，表示这些大米因其浓郁的香气而“闻名”或“为人所知”。

53.note: 修饰复数可数名词 uses（用途），表示大米有“许多”或“各种各样”的用途（many/various/different）。

54.note: 描述西班牙海鲜饭的烹饪方法，指大米“和”海鲜一起烹煮。

55.note: 主语为单数名词 rice，构成地道固定习语 play a key role in，表示在某些甜点中“扮演着关键角色/起着重要作用”，动词需用单三形式 plays。

56.note: 后文有比较连词 than，根据后文它未经过精制且富含矿物质和纤维，可知糙米通常被认为比白米更“健康”（healthier）。

57.note: 前文对比了糙米与白米的营养差异，后文通过 both（两者都是）进行语意转折，指出它们都是极好的能量来源。位于句首需大写（However/Nevertheless）。

58.note: 用于修饰名词 part，表示大米是许多文化和传统中“重要的”、“巨大的”或“不可或缺的”一部分（big/huge/large/important）。

59.note: 介词 During（在……期间）后接名词。结合后文“祭奠祖先、庆祝丰收”，说明是在“节庆”或“节日”期间（celebrations/festivals）。

60.note: 与前面的否定词 not 连用，构成 not just 或 not merely，意思是“不仅仅是”一粒简单的谷物，起强调作用。

61.note: 原因短语：anxious about the surgery → Due to his anxiety about the surgery；后接 had difficulty sleeping。
61.answer: Due to his anxiety about the surgery, Alex had difficulty sleeping.

62.zh: 艾玛问哥哥他前一晚发生了什么事。
62.note: 间接引语：wh- 问句 what had happened to him the previous night；时态后退。

65.zh: 由于坚持不懈，吉尔考试考得很好。
65.note: 原因短语：persevered → because of her perseverance；结果 did very well for her examinations。
65.answer: Jill did very well for her examinations because of her perseverance.

paragraphs.1: 每逢周六早晨，我都会看妈妈指导她的体操课。她在体育馆里动作如此优美，不难相信她曾是奥运体操选手。但那天有些不一样。熟悉的橡胶垫气味弥漫空中，她却失去了往常的活力。
paragraphs.5: 清晨的阳光从高窗洒入。历年奖牌与奖杯陈列墙上，正中醒目地挂着妈妈 2008 年北京奥运会银牌。我记得小时候她常让我戴上，讲述她登上领奖台的经历。
paragraphs.9: “再来一次，姑娘们！”她喊道，示范了一个简单的侧手翻。
paragraphs.10: 她落地时微微踉跄，却强装笑容。我看见她正努力把重心少放在右脚踝上。学生们没注意到这一点，我却注意到了。正是这只脚踝曾支撑她完成无数套路，如今却似乎在辜负她。
paragraphs.13: 我的思绪回到六岁那年，连前滚翻都不敢做。那时的体育馆显得巨大无比。妈妈会在一旁保护我，双手随时准备接住我。我第一次平衡木比赛摔下来时，她就在垫子边，鼓励我继续。那段记忆依然鲜明——寂静的观众，和我再次站起时颤抖的双腿。
paragraphs.18: “每个伟大的体操运动员都会跌倒，索菲，”她当时轻声说，“但只有最优秀的人会重新站起来。”
paragraphs.20: 体育馆的镜子映着晨光，与多年前一样。我记得看她课后加练，在手上抹粉，在平衡木上练习。她在空中翻腾扭转，仿佛不受重力束缚，把看似不可能的动作做得毫不费力。
paragraphs.24: 如今看她示范间隙按摩脚踝，我明白她近来为何多指导、少示范。她的身体已不如从前。上周医生的话仍在耳边——“骨伤愈合不好”——妈妈只是点头，询问改良训练。那就是她向前看、找办法的方式。
paragraphs.29: “陈教练，”一个小学员喊道，马尾随着兴奋跳动，“能再示范一次后空翻吗？”
paragraphs.31: 我看见妈妈犹豫了一瞬——她从未如此过。一丝痛楚掠过她的脸，短暂得只有熟悉她的人才看得出。还没等她回应，我已走上垫子。
paragraphs.34: “让我来示范，”我说着走到中央。做动作时，我倾注她教的一切——每个动作的控制与优美。眼角余光见她注视着我，有一刻我又成了那个六岁孩子，拼命想让她骄傲。
paragraphs.38: 下一项练习，当她要人示范一套动作时，我又举起了手。
paragraphs.40: “让我示范给他们看，妈妈，”我说着做出她多年前教我的组合。小队员们跟着我做，脸上带着我曾有的那份坚定。我听到妈妈依旧清晰自信地指点，引导下一代体操选手。
paragraphs.44: 课后，学员们去更衣室时，妈妈把我搂进怀里。
paragraphs.46: “你什么时候长这么大了？”她轻声问，声音微微发颤。
paragraphs.49: “我跟最好的学的，”我边帮她收垫子边说，“而且你总说体操在于突破界限、激励他人。也许该由我来激励下一代了。”那一刻我明白，有些传承不必用奖牌来证明价值。

66.note:
1. 题型：摘录词句题——从第一段抄四个英文词的短语，说明妈妈动作不如往常有活力（1 分）。

68.note:

69.note:

1. 题型：文中信息归纳表——六岁与现在对比：各写描述词 + 文中证据（4 分；lines 13–43）。
  2. 六岁：行 13 afraid to even do a forward roll；行 17 trembling legs → 词：scared / afraid；证据照抄关键句。
  3. 现在：行 34–35 示范后空翻 control, the grace；行 40–41 带领学生 → 词：confident；证据：She performed the move gracefully.
  4. 表格：第二列词、第三列证据；行优先、从左到右与 fill 一致。
  5. 失分：只填一词无证据；证据与“现在/六岁”时段不符。

answer.74b: She was afraid to do a forward roll, and when she crashed during her first competition, her legs trembled.

75.note:
1. 题型：人物品质——(a) 用一个词形容妈妈；(b) 用文中证据支持（各 1 分，共 2 分；Study 模式 (a)(b) 各一行填空）。
  2. (a)：伤踝仍授课、示范、问改良训练（行 24–28、34–43）→ resilient（坚韧不拔）。
  3. (b)：Even when her ankle was injured, she did not give up and still wanted to teach and help the younger students.
  4. 失分：(a) 只写“好妈妈”无品质词；(b) 证据与品质词无关。

answer.75b: Even when her ankle was injured, she did not give up and still wanted to teach and help the younger students.
